blocks.text: Job 13 belongs to the sustained debate that follows seven days of shared silence. Job’s friends increasingly explain his suffering as evidence of wrongdoing, while Job rejects that diagnosis. This background clarifies why he objects so sharply to their claims to speak for God and insists on presenting his own case.

Job’s persistence through suffering does not mean that he remains silent or accepts harmful explanations. Across the story, his endurance includes continuing to speak honestly, to resist false accusations, and to seek an answer from God.
